text:
alexa: Hi all — trying to bootstrap on my corp laptop behind the company proxy. asdf plugin installs keep failing with curl/git TLS errors. npm install also fails. Anyone walked through this recently? :thinking:

javier: Hey! Yep, hit this last week. Short checklist: 1) set HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars, 2) configure git http.proxy, 3) for PAC files use cntlm or tinyproxy locally, 4) add corp CA to system trust store.

samir: +1. For mac: I exported both uppercase and lowercase envs in my ~/.zshrc: `export HTTPS_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:3128"` and `export https_proxy="$HTTPS_PROXY"`. Then `git config --global http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:3128`. That fixed asdf plugin installs which use `git clone`.

alexa: thanks — we use an automatic PAC file on the VPN. How did you run a local proxy?

javier: I run cntlm on 3128 and point it at the company proxy listed in the PAC. cntlm handles auth with AD creds. Example cntlm conf: ```
# /usr/local/etc/cntlm.conf
Username alexa
Domain REDWOOD
Password password_or_hash
Auth NTLMv2
Listen 127.0.0.1:3128
Proxy proxy.corp.internal:8080
NoProxy localhost,127.0.0.1
```
Then export HTTP(S)_PROXY to http://127.0.0.1:3128.

zoe: if your asdf plugin install still errors with SSL verify: add the corp root CA to the OS trust chain instead of disabling verification. On mac: `sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain corp-root.crt` (need the crt from security). On Ubuntu add to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and run `sudo update-ca-certificates`.

alexa: got it. npm specifics? I have private registries and 2FA tokens via 1Password.

samir: two things: 1) set npm proxy config `npm config set proxy http://127.0.0.1:3128` and `npm config set https-proxy http://127.0.0.1:3128`. 2) for private registries you can export NPM_TOKEN as env var and run `npm login --registry=https://registry.internal` in CI or set in ~/.npmrc: `//registry.internal/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}`.

javier: we use 1Password CLI for dev tokens — `eval $(op signin myaccount)` then `export NPM_TOKEN=$(op item get "redwood-npm-token" --field token)`. Add that export to your dev dotfiles but be careful not to commit.

alexa: re git creds — we have Git Credential Manager installed by default? I'm on mac with Homebrew.

zoe: yes, we use gcm-core. Install: `brew install --cask git-credential-manager-core` or via package. Then `git-credential-manager-core configure` and it will hook into git. For corp SSO you might need to allow the app in security preferences. If gcm prompts you for a browser SSO and it fails behind the proxy, run `GCM_HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:3128 git clone ...` to let GCM use the proxy.

alexa: oof, had an error where VS Code integrated terminal couldn't see my exports from .zshrc. Debug tips?

samir: In VS Code check Terminal > Integrated > Shell Args and make sure login shells are used (e.g., `-l`). Also check VS Code is launched from Finder vs `code` CLI — launching from Finder won't source your shell rc sometimes. I usually `open -a "Visual Studio Code"` after adding a small wrapper that sources dotfiles.

javier: Another gotcha: asdf shims require `eval "$(asdf init -)"` in your rc before PATH changes from other tools. If that's missing, node/python versions not found. Put it near top of .zshrc.

zoe: and for dotfiles that need secrets, we add a `~/.local.env` gitignored file and in repo `.envrc` we load it with direnv. Example `~/.local.env`: `NPM_TOKEN=... GIT_EMAIL="alexa@redwood.com"`. direnv gives nice safety.

alexa: awesome. any commands I should run now to validate everything?

samir: Quick smoke test: ```
# start cntlm
brew services start cntlm
# export proxies
export HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:3128
export HTTPS_PROXY=$HTTP_PROXY
# verify git over proxy
git -c http.proxy=$HTTP_PROXY clone https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf.git /tmp/asdf-test
# verify npm
npm ping
# asdf install shim
asdf plugin-add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git && asdf install nodejs latest
```

alexa: will try these now. thanks all! :pray:

infra-bot: FYI — new-hires checklist updated with a 'proxy & corp CA' troubleshooting section: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboarding/proxy-setup :page_facing_up: 

alexa: nice, saw that — thanks infra-bot :thumbsup:
